title: cardinals try maintain slim playoff chances matchup against spoiler giants  flm 2026 09 09
text:
September 9 - St. Louis will have to figure out a way to slow down Rafael Devers and Bryce Eldridge when the Cardinals attempt to avoid a three-game road sweep by the San Francisco Giants on Wednesday afternoon.
One night after teaming with Devers for ​three doubles and four RBIs in a 5-4, 11-inning win, Eldridge took matters into his own hands ‌in the rematch Tuesday, launching a first-inning solo home run that gave the Giants the early lead in a 2-1 victory.
The consecutive one-run defeats against a non-contender might have sealed the postseason fate of the Cardinals (72-74), who are six games out of the final National League wild-card spot with ​just 16 games remaining.
Monday's starting pitcher for St. Louis, Michael McGreevy, insisted his club was not ready to give ​up the fight.
"Our guys work so hard," he told reporters. "It's a never-say-die team. These guys grind ⁠their (butts) off."
The Giants have been eliminated from postseason contention, and the Cardinals are not far behind. According to ESPN's analytics, the ​Cardinals have less than a 1% chance of making the playoffs.
The consecutive wins not only have given the Giants (61-85) a chance ​to play spoiler, but also have put the team a win away from its first three-game home sweep of the season.
San Francisco will send right-hander Blade Tidwell (0-2, 4.43 ERA) to the mound in search of his first win with the Giants, opposed by St. Louis right-hander Andre Pallante (12-6, 3.51).
Tidwell, ​who grew up about 350 miles southeast of St. Louis in Columbia, Tenn., made his major league debut against the Cardinals ​at Busch Stadium last May for the New York Mets, allowing six runs in 3 2/3 innings. He left the game with a 14.73 ‌ERA.
Pallante, meanwhile, ⁠has gone head-to-head with the Giants eight times, four times as a starter. He's 1-0 with a 5.16 ERA in those games, during which he's seen Eldridge only two times, walking him once and striking him out.
The 27-year-old has gone head-to-head with Devers 12 times, hitting him once, walking him once and allowing two hits, including a home run while Devers was with the ​Boston Red Sox last April.
Pallante ​likely has never seen Devers ⁠as hot as he's been in the Giants' past nine games. Even after going 0-for-4 on Tuesday, Devers has 12 hits in his past 33 at-bats (.364) with six homers and nine walks (two ​intentional).
Eldridge, who has been slotted immediately behind Devers on most nights, said that dynamic has ​helped both left-handed ⁠sluggers.
"I feel very blessed to be able to watch what he's doing from the on-deck circle. It's the closest spot in the park," the rookie said in a television interview shortly after Tuesday's win. "We've kinda just fed off of each other. He feeds me confidence; ⁠hopefully, I ​do the same for him.
"He's given everyone confidence. He shows everyone when he ​goes up there: This is what it looks like. The way he's playing has taken the pressure off everyone. Watching 'The Raffy Show' ... It gives me more ​confidence hitting behind him."
The 21-year-old has hits in 19 of his past 22 games, raising his season average from .245 to .265.
--Field Level Media
